chunks: Al-Husayn b. Ahmad b. Idris (may Allah have mercy on him) narrated to us. He said: My father narrated to us. He said: Abu Sa'id al-Adami narrated to me. He said: al-Hasan b. Ali b. al-Nu'man narrated to me from Ali b. Asbat from al-Hasan b. al-Jahm. He said:

I asked al-Rida (peace be upon him); I said to him: May I be your sacrifice! What is the limit of reliance on Allah (tawakkul)? So he said to me: That you not fear anyone besides Allah. He said: I said: Then what is the limit of humility? He said: That you give to the people of yourself that which you would like to be given. He said: I said: May I be your sacrifice! I desire to know — how am I in your view? So he said: Look to how I am in your view.

key_terms.حَدُّ التَّوَكُّلِ: The limit of reliance on Allah

ai.seo_question: What is the definition of tawakkul and humility according to Imam al-Rida?
ai.summary: Al-Hasan b. al-Jahm asks Imam al-Rida (as) to define two key spiritual concepts. The Imam defines tawakkul (reliance on Allah) as not fearing anyone besides Allah, and humility as giving to others what one would wish to receive. When al-Hasan asks about his status with the Imam, al-Rida responds with a mirror-like teaching: look to what the Imam's status is in your own heart. This exchange would have been understood by the original audience as instruction from the living Imam on essential inner virtues.
